answer: Use network-latency triangulation: each identity must run on distinct hardware in a distinct place. Beacons ping the agent at random times and compare round-trip times; one machine hosting many puppets returns near-identical patterns, like a single tide carrying the same anchor to many supposed shores - a mirror image repeated, not real diversity. A sybil farmer must rent scattered machines to fake the spread, paying real hosting cost per puppet. Limits: VPNs blur the map, shared NAT makes honest agents look alike, congestion adds noise - one layer only, never sole proof.
